correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the exact full three-dimensional vector field and normal defect Qdot=-alpha epsilon Q+(2/epsilon)y(x+yz), whose nullcline value is 2y(epsilon*x+y^3-y)/epsilon^2. On the nullcline z and y^2 stay constant along any contained full orbit; continuity and xdot=y force the unique complete contained orbit to be (0,0,-1/epsilon). For delta=1/epsilon, fast normal derivative -alpha<0 at z=0 and a smooth compact annulus near radius 2/sqrt(3) supports an attracting locally invariant slow graph. Its invariance equation yields h1=y^2-1 and h2=2xy/alpha. The first-order energy-average gives radial F=r(4-3r^2)/8 and simple attracting zero r*=2/sqrt(3), Fprime=-1; first-order averaging plus normal contraction imply an asymptotically stable full-system periodic orbit for sufficiently large epsilon, fixed alpha>0. The compact-annulus boundary can be handled through standard local graph extension. Fresh symbolic algebra separately verified Qdot, h1/h2, F and Fprime; finite computations are only corroboration, not the existence proof. No explicit epsilon0(alpha) or global classification follows.

value.rationale: The research identifies and mathematically repairs a specific defective invariant-manifold step in a primary published dynamics theorem for an exact, natural nonlinear thermostat oscillator. The corrected proof resolves the paper's ambiguity between torus and stable cycle by establishing a definite attracting full-system periodic orbit for every sufficiently large dissipation, and supplies the first nontrivial order of the true slow graph. This has a motivated role in rigorous bifurcation analysis and interpretation of the source's reduced model, not just a cheap numerical countercheck. The radius 2/sqrt(3) and general averaging/Fenichel tools are pre-existing and are not claimed novel.
